resources.string: Two toy boxers, one ring. Win rounds by landing more clean punches than your rival, or knock them down for good.
Jab is fast and light. Hook is slow and heavy, but a yellow ! warns you it is coming. Hold Block to guard, tap Dodge to slip a hook.
A jab cancels a punch that is still winding up. A well-timed dodge makes a hook miss and leaves your rival open to a counter.
Every punch costs stamina. Mash the pads and you will tire out: tired boxers cannot punch and hit softly.
Knocked down? Tap fast to get up before the count reaches ten. Prefer to take it slowly? Turn on Turn-based assist.
Boxing\'s ten-count comes from the Queensberry rules of 1867: a boxer who is down must be back on their feet before ten is counted.
Every pitch is a duel. The pitcher secretly picks a pitch and a spot; the batter secretly picks a swing.
Pitches differ in speed: fastball, slider, curveball and changeup. The middle 3x3 of the grid is the strike zone.
As the batter, choose which pitch you are ready for and where to aim. Match both for a hard hit; miss them and you whiff, foul or ground out.
Four balls are a walk, three strikes are an out, and three outs end the half-inning. The pitch history shows what your rival likes to do.
Play 3, 5 or 9 innings. The home side wins on the spot if it takes the lead in the last inning.
A curveball bends because of its spin: the seams make the air push the ball sideways and down.
